analysis_md:
# AFG — American Financial Group, Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-18. In scope (market cap $12.452B at $149.13, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, fundamentals.json or statements.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Cincinnati-based insurance holding company (roots 1872) operating through Great American Insurance Group: a diversified specialty property & casualty platform of roughly 36 niche commercial businesses (property, transportation, casualty, specialty financial, crop), plus a large investment portfolio ($17.1B at Q2 2026 per company reporting). The annuity business was sold in 2021; this is now a pure specialty P&C story with disciplined, opportunistic capital return (special dividends are a recurring feature).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,533M; net income $842M; SBC $18M (always a real cost); capex $0 — by filing override, see OVERRIDE.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $1.515B = $18.14/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE/share $18.14, latest FY OE total $1.515B).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $928M — essentially net income ($842M) plus D&A ($86M), and it sits far below the OCF-based $1,515M. That gap is the float warning in one line: the OCF definition counts premium/reserve cash that belongs to policyholders first.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Net debt $93.0M (key_numbers.md) — trivial at parent level; the real liabilities are insurance reserves, not debt (total liabilities $27.8B against equity $4,820M at FY2025, fundamentals.json; principal long-term debt $1,848M, debt to total capital 27.5% at FY2025 per the Q1 2026 10-Q).
- Returns since FY-end support the run rate: Q2 2026 core net operating earnings $234M ($2.82/share, +32% YoY), record Q2 pretax P&C operating income $350M, Specialty combined ratio 91.5%, net written premiums +6% YoY, annualized core operating ROE 19.2% (company release, 2026-08-04). Management also agreed to sell the Charleston Harbor Resort & Marina for an expected ~$125M pretax core gain (~$1.20/share) — a noncore asset, not underwriting earnings.

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $1,533M − prior YTD $533M + current YTD $566M = **TTM $1,566M**
- SBC: FY $18M − prior YTD $8,926,027 + current YTD $8,926,027 = **TTM $18M** (both YTD legs filled by the sbc_override — AFG tags SBC only annually; see OVERRIDE)
- Capex: **TTM $0**, all three legs filled by the override (see OVERRIDE)
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **83,100,000**
- **TTM OE total $1,548M → base OE/share $18.63** (base_source: ttm_json)

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: a diversified specialty P&C franchise (~36 niche businesses via Great American) with a combined ratio better than the industry for more than two decades and sustained high returns, but insurance capacity is close to a commodity — no network effects, modest switching costs, price set by the cycle — and social inflation / catastrophe / alternative-investment returns can erase a year of underwriting profit.
- Evidence first (fundamentals.json): the `roic_proxy` series (after-tax operating income over equity + debt − cash) is 17.3% (FY2025), 19.6% (FY2024) and 18.8% (FY2023) — well above a cost of capital through this stretch — and ROE is 17.5% / 19.9% / 20.0% over the same years. Gross margin is not computable or meaningful for an insurer (no COGS is filed); the underwriting substitute is the combined ratio: 91.5% in Q2 2026 and better than the industry average for more than two decades per company/Zacks reporting. Caveat stated plainly: both ROIC-proxy and ROE are float-levered for an insurer, which is why this earns a 5, not a 7+.
- FOR: diversified specialty P&C platform (~36 niche businesses) with granular underwriting expertise in hard-to-insure commercial niches; combined ratio better than the industry average for more than two decades, 91.5% in Q2 2026; sustained returns (roic_proxy 17.3-19.6% and ROE 17.5-20.0% in FY2023-25, fundamentals.json); pricing power in the current cycle — renewal rate increases ~5% ex workers' comp for four consecutive quarters through Q2 2026; disciplined capital allocation — $707M returned in FY2025 including $334M of special dividends, debt/total capital 27.5%.
- AGAINST: insurance capacity is close to a commodity — no network effects, low switching costs, pricing set by a softening industry cycle; social inflation on U.S. casualty lines and catastrophe exposure can produce reserve charges that erase underwriting profit; earnings depend materially on investment returns including alternatives (7.1% annualized in Q2 2026 vs a 10%+ long-term target) — volatile and market-driven; crop seasonality concentrates profitability in Q4 and workers' comp pricing was down ~2% in Q2 2026.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (NI vs OCF differ by >40% in 2023 and 2025): structural insurer float, not a one-off error in either series. FY2023: net income $852M vs OCF $1,970M in a year revenue grew 11.2% — premiums collected and loss/unearned-premium reserves built ahead of claims paid are operating cash in excess of earned profit. FY2025: net income $842M vs OCF $1,533M on the same mechanism (reserves and unearned premiums up with the book), and the TTM window repeats it (NI $953M vs OCF $1,566M, fundamentals.json). Resolution: neither series is wrong, but an OCF base on a growing insurer capitalizes float, which is exactly Andrew's insurer-float case — the tier is softened one notch (verdict below) and confidence is low. Note the divergence is NOT explained by reserve charges here (AFG has no EG-style charge in these years); it is growth float, the milder but still disqualifying-for-full-credit form.
